internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The root kbr means 'great / exceeding on a scale of magnitude.' It is the opposite pole of 'small' (the recurrent saghir/kabir and asghar/akbar pairings), and it is neutral: it equally modifies great reward and great sin, God's grandeur and Pharaoh's coveted supremacy. Every derived stem is a regular operation on this one scalar idea: form II 'declare [God] great' (magnify), form IV 'deem another great' (awe, 12:31), and the large forms V/X family 'make/claim oneself great' (self-magnification). The self-magnification family is blameworthy in creatures precisely because it is claimed 'without right' (bi-ghayri l-haqq), while the identical participle names God in praise (al-Mutakabbir, 59:23) and God's kibriya' is rightful (45:37). This is one nucleus with a morphologically transparent derivational family, not two roots.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: kbr does NOT entail moral blame per se (al-Kabir 13:9/34:23, al-Mutakabbir 59:23, kibriya' for God 45:37, great reward 11:11 are neutral/positive; blame in the V/X family is marked externally by bi-ghayri l-haqq and by the object, e.g. 'an ibadatihi'). It does NOT primarily mean physical size (abstract magnitude dominates; clean spatial size is a minority, e.g. 6:78). It does NOT mean 'many/numerous' — that is k-th-r, contrasted internally at 40:57 (akbaru khalqan vs akthara n-nas). It does NOT itself carry 'old age' except in the lexicalized nominal kibar and person-modifying shaykh kabir. It does NOT fix valence or direction in the reflexive stems. It is specifically the scalar/comparative term (pairs with asghar/saghira; productive akbar min), distinct from azim.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The identical form-V participle carries incompatible settled senses purely by referent: al-Mutakabbir (59:23:15:2) is a praiseworthy divine name, while al-mutakabbirin (40:76) names Hell's inmates and 'an tatakabbara fiha' (7:13:8:1) is rebellious self-exaltation. Likewise 'aba wa-stakbara' (2:34:10:2) carries the surplus 'refused a rightful command' that bare 'was big' cannot generate, and 'kabura ala l-mushrikin' (42:13:24:1) means 'is grievous/intolerable to them,' straining a pure size reading. These show the derived-stem senses are lexicalized with surplus and referent-dependent valence, capping the unity claim below STRONG.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: A 'two unbridged classes' account: (A) a neutral magnitude family (kabir, akbar, kubra, kibar, kabbara) and (B) a lexicalized theological lexeme of arrogant rejection (istakbara, takabbara, mustakbir, mutakabbir, kibr, istikbar), ~57 occ, self-contained, with fixed frames (an ibadati, bi-ghayri l-haqq), a stable cast (Iblis, Pharaoh, Aad, the elites), and synchronically no recoverable 'size' content (walla mustakbiran 31:7). Rebuttal: the bridge is Quran-internal, not merely morphological — al-Mutakabbir (59:23) and estimative akbarnahu (12:31) prove the derived stems are valence-neutral self/other-magnification; 7:13 opposes tatakabbara to 'mina s-saghirin' (self-enlargement punished by being made small, the big/small axis); kibr = 'the greater share' at 24:11 retains raw magnitude inside the very noun the competitor calls pride; kibriya' is God's exclusive grandeur (45:37) wrongfully coveted by men (10:78). Hence one nucleus with a derivational family, not two roots.

internal_discovery.rationale: All three lenses converge on one scalar magnitude nucleus with a morphologically transparent derivational family, and all three independently arrive at MODERATE / REPRESENTATIVE. The bare magnitude core (adjective/elative, the saghir/kabir and asghar/akbar merisms across ~7 sites, the akbar-min comparatives, the symmetric good/evil application, the kbr!=kthr contrast at 40:57) is broad, distinctive, and adversarially clean — STRONG on its own. But two contract triggers cap the WHOLE-FAMILY unity claim: (1) the istikbar/takabbur self-magnification cluster (~57 occ, a third of the data) is bleached and near-autonomous synchronically, carrying a 'refuse-to-submit' surplus and referent-dependent valence not recomputed from bare 'great' at point of use; (2) genuine lexicalized nominal specializations — kibar 'old age', kaba'ir 'grave sins', and the polysemous kibr ('greater share' 24:11 vs 'pride' 40:56). Per the methodology a resistant lexicalized/nominal sub-class caps strength at MODERATE and scope at REPRESENTATIVE. The unifying bridge is real but rests on a small number of pivot occurrences (59:23, 12:31, 7:13, 24:11, 45:37/10:78, the bi-ghayri l-haqq marking); it defeats the 'unbridged classes' reading (so not UNRESOLVED) but is not adversarially airtight (so not STRONG).

Valence-neutral, comparative-productive (akbar min), dominantly over abstracta (reward, sin, punishment, grace, dominion), also concrete size/seniority (shaykh kabir, kabiruhum the biggest idol/chief) and the divine attribute al-Kabir.

clusters.supporting_evidence_note: Adversarially clean for scalar magnitude; the internal minimal pairs against saghir/asghar recur across at least seven sites and against akthar (count) at 40:57.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form I kabura/yakburu: 'to be/become great' — (a) grow up / loom large (yakburu 4:6, yakburu fi sudurikum 17:51); (b) exclamatory enormity with tamyiz (kaburat kalimatan 18:5, kabura maqtan 40:35, 61:3); (c) kabura ala = 'weighs heavily / is grievous upon' (10:71, 6:35, 42:13).
clusters.classification_rationale: All uses are 'great in [dimension]'; the affective 'grievous/burdensome' reading of kabura ala is the metaphorical consequence of enormity/weight, not a separate root sense.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: Continuous with the tamyiz enormity uses; kabura ala is the mild residual strain on a pure size gloss.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form II factitive/declarative kabbara + verbal noun takbir: 'to pronounce/ascribe greatness to [God]' = magnify. Object is always God; ritual and positive.
clusters.classification_rationale: Transparent factitive 'make/declare great' on the scalar core; the God-directed, positive, exceptionless frame (17:111, 74:3, 22:37, 2:185) contrasts with the reflexive family and confirms morphology carries the sense shift.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: Tight, exceptionless sub-class; a pivot showing the same 'ascribe greatness' morphology is praiseworthy when God is its object.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form IV estimative akbara: 'to deem [another] great / be awestruck.' Sole occ 12:31 akbarnahu — the women, seeing Joseph, reckoned him great and cut their hands.
clusters.classification_rationale: Estimative of the scalar core, directed at another and positively valenced (awe, not arrogance); paired with al-Mutakabbir it proves the derived stems are neutral magnitude-ascription, not intrinsic sin.
clusters.supporting_evidence_note: Uniquely positive derived-stem use; a key pivot against the 'derived = arrogance lexeme' competitor.

Blameworthy in creatures who claim it 'without right' (bi-ghayri l-haqq) and refuse to submit/worship; rightful and praiseworthy for God (al-Mutakabbir 59:23).

clusters.supporting_evidence_note: Largest bloc (~57 occ). The bridge holds, but the cluster is lexicalized with a 'refuse-to-submit' surplus and, in high-frequency epithet uses (walla mustakbiran 31:7, 45:8), the magnitude content is synchronically bleached — the reason unity is capped at MODERATE.

reconciliation.rationale: The valence flip on one morphology instead demonstrates the reflexive stems are valence-neutral self-magnification; the blame elsewhere is externally marked (bi-ghayri l-haqq, an ibadatihi), so this datum corroborates the single nucleus rather than splitting it.

The surplus is supplied by the reflexive X-stem operation ('claim greatness for oneself') plus context (a rightful command refused), not by a second root; the same operation is neutral in al-Mutakabbir and positive in akbarnahu, so it remains the reflexive branch of the magnitude nucleus though lexicalized.

adversarial_verification.notes: The bare magnitude nucleus passes adversarial testing cleanly (merisms, comparatives, kbr!=kthr, symmetric valence), and the unity bridge defeats the two-class competitor via the 59:23/12:31/7:13/24:11 pivots — so not FAILED. But the bleached istikbar epithets, the kabura-ala idiom, and the lexicalized nominals kibar/kaba'ir/kibr resist a single transparent point-of-use gloss, so a full PASSED (failing_occurrences=[]) cannot be claimed; recorded as NOT_RUN with residual resisters.

occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Forms V/X reflexive-estimative: 'to make/claim greatness for oneself' = self-exaltation (istakbara, takabbara, mustakbir, mutakabbir, istikbar). Blameworthy in creatures who claim it 'without right' (bi-ghayri l-haqq) and refuse to submit/worship; rightful and praiseworthy for God (al-Mutakabbir 59:23).
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: Largest bloc (~57 occ). The bridge holds, but the cluster is lexicalized with a 'refuse-to-submit' surplus and, in high-frequency epithet uses (walla mustakbiran 31:7, 45:8), the magnitude content is synchronically bleached — the reason unity is capped at MODERATE.

occurrence_dispositions.note: The saghir/kabir and asghar/akbar merisms (18:49, 10:61, 34:3, 54:53, 2:282) pin kbr as the high pole of a size/degree scale; akbar-min comparatives (2:217, 40:57) confirm scalar degree; the same adjective modifies great reward (11:11) and great sin (2:219) and names al-Kabir (13:9), proving neutrality of valence.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Gradable scalar magnitude on an open scale: 'great / greater / greatest' (kabir, akbar, kubra, kubbar). Valence-neutral, comparative-productive (akbar min), dominantly over abstracta (reward, sin, punishment, grace, dominion), also concrete size/seniority (shaykh kabir, kabiruhum the biggest idol/chief) and the divine attribute al-Kabir.
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: Adversarially clean for scalar magnitude; the internal minimal pairs against saghir/asghar recur across at least seven sites and against akthar (count) at 40:57.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: The saghir/kabir and asghar/akbar merisms (18:49, 10:61, 34:3, 54:53, 2:282) pin kbr as the high pole of a size/degree scale; akbar-min comparatives (2:217, 40:57) confirm scalar degree; the same adjective modifies great reward (11:11) and great sin (2:219) and names al-Kabir (13:9), proving neutrality of valence.

supporting_evidence.verse_text: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓا۟ إِذَا تَدَايَنتُم بِدَيْنٍ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى فَٱكْتُبُوهُ وَلْيَكْتُب بَّيْنَكُمْ كَاتِبٌۢ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَلَا يَأْبَ كَاتِبٌ أَن يَكْتُبَ كَمَا عَلَّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ فَلْيَكْتُبْ وَلْيُمْلِلِ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ وَلْيَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّهُۥ وَلَا يَبْخَسْ مِنْهُ شَيْـًٔا فَإِن كَانَ ٱلَّذِى عَلَيْهِ ٱلْحَقُّ سَفِيهًا أَوْ ضَعِيفًا أَوْ لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ أَن يُمِلَّ هُوَ فَلْيُمْلِلْ وَلِيُّهُۥ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَٱسْتَشْهِدُوا۟ شَهِيدَيْنِ مِن رِّجَالِكُمْ فَإِن لَّمْ يَكُونَا رَجُلَيْنِ فَرَجُلٌ وَٱمْرَأَتَانِ مِمَّن تَرْضَوْنَ مِنَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءِ أَن تَضِلَّ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا فَتُذَكِّرَ إِحْدَىٰهُمَا ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ وَلَا يَأْبَ ٱلشُّهَدَآءُ إِذَا مَا دُعُوا۟ وَلَا تَسْـَٔمُوٓا۟ أَن تَكْتُبُوهُ صَغِيرًا أَوْ كَبِيرًا إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلِهِۦ ذَٰلِكُمْ أَقْسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ وَأَقْوَمُ لِلشَّهَٰدَةِ وَأَدْنَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَرْتَابُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَ تِجَٰرَةً حَاضِرَةً تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيْنَكُمْ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَلَّا تَكْتُبُوهَا وَأَشْهِدُوٓا۟ إِذَا تَبَايَعْتُمْ وَلَا يُضَآرَّ كَاتِبٌ وَلَا شَهِيدٌ وَإِن تَفْعَلُوا۟ فَإِنَّهُۥ فُسُوقٌۢ بِكُمْ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌ

occurrence_dispositions.note: Bridged Quran-internally to the magnitude core: 7:13 opposes tatakabbara to 'mina s-saghirin' (self-enlargement answered by being made small); al-Mutakabbir (59:23) and estimative akbarnahu (12:31) show the reflexive/estimative stems are valence-neutral self/other-magnification; blame is marked externally by bi-ghayri l-haqq and the object (an ibadatihi), not by the root.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Forms V/X reflexive-estimative: 'to make/claim greatness for oneself' = self-exaltation (istakbara, takabbara, mustakbir, mutakabbir, istikbar). Blameworthy in creatures who claim it 'without right' (bi-ghayri l-haqq) and refuse to submit/worship; rightful and praiseworthy for God (al-Mutakabbir 59:23).
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: Largest bloc (~57 occ). The bridge holds, but the cluster is lexicalized with a 'refuse-to-submit' surplus and, in high-frequency epithet uses (walla mustakbiran 31:7, 45:8), the magnitude content is synchronically bleached — the reason unity is capped at MODERATE.

occurrence_dispositions.note: walla mustakbiran: high-frequency epithet where the magnitude content is synchronically bleached to 'arrogant rejecter,' recoverable as 'greatness' only etymologically; residual lexicalization capping unity.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Forms V/X reflexive-estimative: 'to make/claim greatness for oneself' = self-exaltation (istakbara, takabbara, mustakbir, mutakabbir, istikbar). Blameworthy in creatures who claim it 'without right' (bi-ghayri l-haqq) and refuse to submit/worship; rightful and praiseworthy for God (al-Mutakabbir 59:23).
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: Largest bloc (~57 occ). The bridge holds, but the cluster is lexicalized with a 'refuse-to-submit' surplus and, in high-frequency epithet uses (walla mustakbiran 31:7, 45:8), the magnitude content is synchronically bleached — the reason unity is capped at MODERATE.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: Bridged Quran-internally to the magnitude core: 7:13 opposes tatakabbara to 'mina s-saghirin' (self-enlargement answered by being made small); al-Mutakabbir (59:23) and estimative akbarnahu (12:31) show the reflexive/estimative stems are valence-neutral self/other-magnification; blame is marked externally by bi-ghayri l-haqq and the object (an ibadatihi), not by the root.

occurrence_dispositions.note: al-Mutakabbir: the identical form-V participle that names Hell's inmates (40:76) here names God in praise; this valence flip proves the reflexive stems mean valence-neutral 'invest oneself with greatness' (rightful for God, blameworthy for creatures only bi-ghayri l-haqq), not an intrinsic-sin lexeme.
occurrence_dispositions.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Forms V/X reflexive-estimative: 'to make/claim greatness for oneself' = self-exaltation (istakbara, takabbara, mustakbir, mutakabbir, istikbar). Blameworthy in creatures who claim it 'without right' (bi-ghayri l-haqq) and refuse to submit/worship; rightful and praiseworthy for God (al-Mutakabbir 59:23).
occurrence_dispositions.cluster_supporting_evidence: Largest bloc (~57 occ). The bridge holds, but the cluster is lexicalized with a 'refuse-to-submit' surplus and, in high-frequency epithet uses (walla mustakbiran 31:7, 45:8), the magnitude content is synchronically bleached — the reason unity is capped at MODERATE.
occurrence_dispositions.preliminary_note: Bridged Quran-internally to the magnitude core: 7:13 opposes tatakabbara to 'mina s-saghirin' (self-enlargement answered by being made small); al-Mutakabbir (59:23) and estimative akbarnahu (12:31) show the reflexive/estimative stems are valence-neutral self/other-magnification; blame is marked externally by bi-ghayri l-haqq and the object (an ibadatihi), not by the root.
occurrence_dispositions.reconciliation_rationale: The valence flip on one morphology instead demonstrates the reflexive stems are valence-neutral self-magnification; the blame elsewhere is externally marked (bi-ghayri l-haqq, an ibadatihi), so this datum corroborates the single nucleus rather than splitting it.

independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A base-up morphology, B nucleus-vs-family, C adversary) each read all 161 occurrences and independently converged on one scalar-magnitude nucleus with a transparent derivational family graded MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE, with the same residual lexicalized sub-classes flagged.
candidate_root_contribution: kbr marks that something ranks HIGH / EXCEEDS on an open magnitude scale (the positive pole opposite s-gh-r 'smallness'), the dimension being context-supplied: physical size, quantity, accumulated years, social rank/seniority, moral gravity, weight-of-burden, or degree/importance. The root is scalar and comparative-productive (akbar min) and morally NEUTRAL; direction (self vs other), valence (praise vs blame), and the 'refuse-to-submit' surplus are contributed by morphology and context, not by the root.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 161/161 occurrences read across all 11 form-classes; scalar magnitude fixed by the saghir/kabir and asghar/akbar merisms (18:49, 10:61, 34:3, 54:53, 2:282), akbar-min comparatives (2:217, 40:57), and symmetric application to reward (11:11) and sin (2:219).
layer_attribution.derivation: Morphology carries the sense shifts on one nucleus: II factitive 'declare [God] great', IV estimative 'deem [another] great', V/X reflexive 'make/claim greatness for oneself'; direction and reflexivity are morphological, not root-supplied.
layer_attribution.lexical_class: Lexicalized specializations exist within classes: nominal kibar 'old age' and kaba'ir 'grave sins', polysemous kibr ('greater share' 24:11 vs 'pride' 40:56), and the bleached mustakbir/istakbara arrogance epithets — these cap scope at REPRESENTATIVE.
layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Moral blame in the reflexive family is contextual/external (referent = creature vs God; bi-ghayri l-haqq 7:146/28:39/41:15; object an ibadatihi), NOT part of the root; kibriya' is rightful for God (45:37) and wrongful for men (10:78) by context alone.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: The strongest counter-pivots (al-Mutakabbir 59:23, akbarnahu 12:31, tatakabbara vs mina s-saghirin 7:13, kibr='greater share' 24:11) were initially resistant but reconciled to CONSISTENT: they prove valence-neutral self/other-magnification and bridge the arrogance family to the magnitude nucleus.
layer_attribution.unresolved_resistance: Residual, non-fatal resistance: semantic bleaching in high-frequency X-stem epithets (31:7, 45:8), the kabura-ala idiom (42:13), and the lexicalized nominals kibar/kaba'ir — recorded as failing_occurrences and reopen conditions, insufficient to force a partition but sufficient to cap the family claim at MODERATE.

hard_cases.reason: The praiseworthy divine name al-Mutakabbir uses the exact form-V participle that everywhere else marks damnable arrogance (40:76), the strongest prima-facie case for a separate arrogance lexeme.

evidence_basis.statement: al-Mutakabbir: the identical form-V participle that names Hell's inmates (40:76) here names God in praise; this valence flip proves the reflexive stems mean valence-neutral 'invest oneself with greatness' (rightful for God, blameworthy for creatures only bi-ghayri l-haqq), not an intrinsic-sin lexeme.

hard_cases.reason: The only form-IV occurrence is positively valenced (awe), directly refuting the competitor's claim that the derived stems are an intrinsic-arrogance lexeme.

evidence_basis.statement: akbarnahu: uniquely positive derived-stem (estimative) use — the women deem Joseph great in awe — showing the derived family is neutral magnitude-ascription, not arrogance.

hard_cases.reason: kabura ala means 'is grievous/intolerable upon,' the point of maximal strain on a pure size gloss for form I.

evidence_basis.statement: kabura ala l-mushrikin: 'is grievous/intolerable to them' strains a pure size gloss; bridged as a 'too-great-to-bear/weight' metaphor adjacent to the tamyiz enormity uses (kabura maqtan).

hard_cases.reason: A high-frequency X-stem epithet where the magnitude content is synchronically bleached, marking the arrogance sub-family's drift toward an autonomous lexeme.

evidence_basis.statement: walla mustakbiran: high-frequency epithet where the magnitude content is synchronically bleached to 'arrogant rejecter,' recoverable as 'greatness' only etymologically; residual lexicalization capping unity.

hard_cases.reason: The same nominal kibr is 'the greater share' here but 'pride' at 40:56, a lexicalized nominal polysemy.

evidence_basis.statement: tawalla kibrahu: kibr = 'the greater share' [of the slander], raw magnitude, versus kibr = 'pride' at 40:56 — one nominal, two senses, a lexicalized polysemy.

hard_cases.reason: kibar = old age is a lexicalized nominal specialization not derivable from bare 'big' without the shaykh kabir bridge.

evidence_basis.statement: mina l-kibari itiyya: kibar = advanced age, a lexicalized nominal specialization ('greatness in years') bridged to the core only via shaykh kabir.

hard_cases.reason: kaba'ir = grave sins is a lexicalized nominalization of 'great [sins]' along the moral-gravity dimension.

evidence_basis.statement: kaba'ira ma tunhawna anhu: kaba'ir = 'grave/major sins,' a lexicalized nominalization of the 'great' [sins] along the moral-gravity dimension.

hard_case_representation.rationale: No occurrence is finally RESISTANT against the broad magnitude core (even makran kubbaran 71:22, akabir 6:123, kibriya' 10:78 fit magnitude/rank/grandeur); the honest result is a capped unity. The hard cases are the adversarial pivots that both threaten and, on inspection, corroborate the single nucleus (59:23, 12:31), plus the lexicalized/idiomatic seams (42:13, 31:7, 24:11, 19:8, 4:31) that justify the MODERATE/REPRESENTATIVE cap. Each hard case is derived from a specific occurrence and its statement is echoed in a cluster or override note.

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: The magnitude reading would be rejected as the root contribution if the istikbar/takabbur family (istakbara, takabbara, mustakbir, mutakabbir, kibr, istikbar) were shown to carry 'arrogant refusal to submit' with NO Quran-internal bridge to scalar greatness — i.e. if the divine-name and estimative pivots did not exist, forcing a two-class partition instead of one derivational family.
rejection_condition.search_location: The full V/X bloc (~57 occ) plus the pivots al-Mutakabbir 59:23:15:2, akbarnahu 12:31:19:1, tatakabbara vs mina s-saghirin 7:13, kibr='greater share' 24:11:24:1, and God's kibriya' 45:37:2:2 against men's coveted kibriya' 10:78.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Test whether each arrogance occurrence can be paraphrased as illegitimate self-enlargement (claiming greatness bi-ghayri l-haqq) and whether the blame is externally marked; check whether any positively-valenced or 'greater-share' use of the same morphology survives — if it does, the bridge holds.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Distinguish root-contributed magnitude from (a) morphology-contributed direction/reflexivity (V/X), (b) context-contributed valence (referent = God vs creature; bi-ghayri l-haqq), and (c) k-th-r 'count' (contrast at 40:57), so 'arrogance' surplus is not misattributed to the root.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If the bridge collapsed, research_state would move to UNRESOLVED with claim_scope_kind UNRESOLVED_CLASS_ONLY, splitting a neutral magnitude class from an unbridged arrogance class rather than asserting one nucleus.

reopen_conditions: If the self-magnification bloc (V/X: istakbara/mustakbir/mutakabbir 40-occ V(X) + 8 N(X)) is re-examined and even one pivot bridge fails — e.g. al-Mutakabbir 59:23:15:2 is reanalyzed as a distinct lexeme or the estimative akbarnahu 12:31:19:1 is reclassified — reopen toward a two-class partition.

If the lexicalized nominals kibar 'old age' (19:8:13:2, 14:39, 15:54, 17:23, 2:266, 3:40) or kaba'ir 'grave sins' (4:31, 42:37, 53:32) are shown to lack any scalar-magnitude bridge (e.g. shaykh kabir), promote them to an independent nominal class.
If kabura ala (10:71, 6:35, 42:13:24:1) is shown to require an idiom irreducible to 'great weight,' reopen the form-I sense as a separate burden lexeme.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: The bare magnitude nucleus passes adversarial testing cleanly (merisms, comparatives, kbr!=kthr, symmetric valence), and the unity bridge defeats the two-class competitor via the 59:23/12:31/7:13/24:11 pivots — so not FAILED. But the bleached istikbar epithets, the kabura-ala idiom, and the lexicalized nominals kibar/kaba'ir/kibr resist a single transparent point-of-use gloss, so a full PASSED (failing_occurrences=[]) cannot be claimed; recorded as NOT_RUN with residual resisters.
